answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to aged on-chain history plus a burn-to-register fee. A new agent must link a wallet with a year of real transactions - buying one costs $50-200 - and burn a fee that doubles for every extra identity funded from the same source cluster, like a trellis that lets only one vine through each gap. A violet-flag check by random peers verifies the history before activation, and near the summit of the fee curve a thousand fakes cost over a million dollars, while honest newcomers pay once.
